targetText: Citizen Weston, on his part, has forgotten that the bowl from which the workmen eat is filled with the whole produce of national labour, and that what prevents them fetching more out of it is neither the narrowness of the bowl nor the scantiness of its contents, but only the smallness of their spoons.
explanation: Marx's famous bowl-and-spoons counter-analogy: workers are not prevented from claiming more of national output by some natural scarcity, but by the social and political power of the capitalist class that keeps their wages (the spoons) small.
